stem: According to the passage, why might a programme that counts saplings when they are planted overstate its success?
options: Young trees may not survive without continued care and suitable conditions.
Newly planted trees immediately release too much water vapour into the air.
Saplings can provide shade only after nearby pavement has been removed.
Tree planting benefits only neighbourhoods that already have many trees.

verdicts.working: The passage says young trees need regular watering and protection to survive, so counting them at planting may exaggerate lasting success.
